title: Shader and material assignment per patch label
description: 'Should be able to apply shaders to patch labels.' Add `set_label_material(geometry, label, shader, colour, params)` writing a per-label material assignment into the CRAW-3 material slot (label -> MaterialData/shader id), and teach HalfEdgeMeshRuntime to partition the index buffer by label the way TagRange partitions by tag today (generalize TagRange into a draw-range group with its own ShaderProgram/uniforms), binding a different shader per group (e.g. flat, lit, textured, rim-lit, chitin-like specular for the crawfish shell). Unlabelled faces fall through to the default material. Draw order stays deterministic (sorted by label). Related: VIEW-1 (per-vertex color shader), VIEW-2 (tag color mapping), VIEW-5 (tagged rendering pipeline) -- generalize their tag colouring into label materials instead of a parallel path.
definition-of-done: 1. set_label_material node registered and documented; catalog regenerated. 2. HalfEdgeMeshRuntime renders two labels with two visibly different shaders in the patch-label scene (screenshot). 3. Faces under a child label inherit the parent's material unless overridden. 4. Per-frame draw does not allocate; groups rebuild only when labels/materials change. 5. Existing setTags/FLAT/SCALAR modes unchanged (regression screenshots on mesh-boolean scene). 6. Build checkstyle-green.
testing-plan: 1. Unit: material assignment resolution (own label > parent > default) on a hand-built PatchLabels. 2. Unit (headless GL): draw-range grouping produces contiguous ranges covering every face exactly once. 3. run-scene patch-label with a test graph assigning 'claw' textured and 'tail' rim-lit; screenshot.
todos: Generalize TagRange into a label/material draw group with shader reference
Implement set_label_material node and material slot extension
Inheritance resolution through the label hierarchy
unknowns: Whether per-group shader switching is acceptable cost or materials should be one uber-shader with per-face material index attribute
How label materials compose with the CRAW-3 photographic base-colour texture (multiply? override?)
